priceSnapshot.note: PROVENANCE, and the same warning as the last three sessions with one new wrinkle. The run's web_fetch proxy served a FRESH spot ticker this time but STALE derivatives: open interest stamped 2026-09-08T17:18:33Z (13h 49m old), funding stamped 15:20:03Z (15h 47m old) and an hourly account-ratio bucket 14h 7m old, and the 1H candle set came back with its newest bar 24 hours behind. All of it was DISCARDED under the freshness guard. Adding a cache-busting query parameter made the candles WORSE, returning a snapshot from 04 September. Every exchange number below was therefore re-pulled in-page against okx.com with cache 'no-store' and each payload timestamp checked against wall clock: spot ticker (0.6s), open interest (0s), funding (50s), the 1H long/short account ratio (68 min, an hourly bucket) and the 100 most recent filled BTC-USDT swap liquidations (newest 1.8 min old). changePct is against the rolling 24h open of 78,407.8. Against end of day's 78,570.0 read, price is 761.4 points HIGHER - plus 0.97 percent across 6h 30m, and the move is not drift: the 78,900.0 add gate end of day wrote down FIRED on the settled 04:00 UTC hourly close of 79,169.0 and has been confirmed by two further settled closes above. The session low of 78,551.3 came 926.7 points above the 77,624.6 reduce gate. For the first time in four sessions one of the two gates fired and was RIGHT.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 78,551.3 - the low of this session, 780.1 points under spot and 2.17 hourly ATRs away. The gate MOVES UP from end of day's 77,624.6, and the justification is that the structure it was protecting has changed. End of day held 77,624.6 because 78,000.0 had whipsawed morning and a tighter gate would have fired on noise; that was correct for a market pinned inside 78,265-78,825. Price has now settled three consecutive hourly candles above 78,900.0 and cleared the 1H EMA100 at 79,117.54, so the thing worth protecting is the reclaim itself, not the old range floor. Losing 78,551.3 on a settled basis means the breakout hour has been fully retraced and the 78,900.0 shelf has flipped back to resistance. Below it there is 286.3 points to the 78,265.0 flush low and then a 640.4-point air pocket to 77,624.6.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 79,648.1 - the 08 September swing high, 316.7 points over spot and 0.88 hourly ATRs away. Spot has already taken the 24h high at 79,396.8, so the next real ceiling is this one. The measured short-side fuel in the 79,200-79,400 strip is SPENT: 414,424 USD of shorts were liquidated across 86 buy fills in the last two hours, and a squeeze that has already run does not push twice. Clearing 79,648.1 on a settled basis is what would prove new buyers rather than covered sellers, and it also puts 80,000.0 and the 80,555.4 high from 07 September in play.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from end of day's HOLD to ADD, and the trigger is end of day's own written condition, not a change of mind. End of day set the add gate at 78,900.0 requiring a settled 1H close above; the 04:00 UTC candle closed at 79,169.0, 269.0 points through, and 05:00 and 06:00 settled at 78,935.1 and 79,160.3. Three consecutive settled closes above a gate that had refused twice in two days is the confirmation end of day asked for and did not get. Spot now trades above every EMA on every timeframe examined - 15m, 1H, 4H and daily, twelve of twelve - which has not been true in this series since 06 September. The 1H MACD histogram has crossed to +92.12 from deeply negative. What holds the position at ADD rather than anything larger is that the positioning that made end of day cautious has NOT eased: open interest is 2,181,780,465 USD against end of day's 2,166,661,931, UP 0.70 percent and reversing two consecutive falls; funding is +0.0000544254651923 against +0.0000481525, UP 13.03 percent; the long/short account ratio is 1.26, unchanged and still crowded long. So the breakout is real and the fuel behind it is already burnt. That combination earns a measured tranche, not the rest of the cash.

liquidation.note: 224,187 USD of SHORT liquidations across 51 buy-side fills - the single largest cluster in the rolling window and the reason it carries magnet=true. These are REALISED fills, not resting orders, executed as price drove through 79,300 into the 79,396.8 high, so the leverage that sat here is already gone. What the cluster maps is where the leveraged SHORT cohort was positioned, 31.4 points under spot. It is the mirror image of what end of day measured six hours ago, when 872,530 USD of longs were flushed at 78,400.

189,818 USD of short liquidations across 35 buy-side fills, 131.4 points under spot. Together with the 79,300 band this is 414,005 USD of short-side stops taken out inside a 200-point strip in under two hours - the fuel that produced the move. It is now spent, which is the main reason this report adds a measured tranche rather than chasing.

63,201 USD of LONG liquidations across 12 sell-side fills, 531.4 points under spot, all of them from the 05:14-05:30 UTC dip to 78,841.7 before the breakout. Small, and the only downside cluster in the window: longs to shorts runs 63,201 against 414,424, a 6.6-to-1 SHORT flush where end of day measured 7.5-to-1 the other way.

ESTIMATED leverage-bracket magnet - not exchange resting-order data. The OKX realised-liquidation window (05:14:49 to 07:07:29 UTC) contains no fills above spot at all, so nothing overhead is measured. This level is the 08 September swing high, which sits inside the 100x short bracket computed as 79,331.4 x (1 + 1/100) = 80,124.7 and is where stops from shorts that survived the 79,200-79,400 flush would sit. Treat it as a structural guess anchored to resistance, not as a reading of the book.

liquidityMagnet.note: MEASURED, fresh, and inverted from end of day. The 100-fill window is unusually tight - 1 hour 53 minutes, 05:14:49 to 07:07:29 UTC, newest fill 1.8 minutes old - which by itself says the tape has been violent. It splits 86 buy-side fills against 12 sell-side: 414,424 USD of SHORTS liquidated against 63,201 USD of longs, a 6.6-to-1 short-side flush. End of day measured 1,809,595 USD of longs against 240,040 USD of shorts, 7.5-to-1 downward. Weighted by price band the entire measured flow now sits at or just below spot in the 79,200-79,400 strip, which is a squeeze that has already resolved rather than a magnet still pulling. pull is set to up because the only unclaimed fuel is overhead and price has just taken the 24h high, but the honest caveat is that this is inference from an empty upper book, not measurement: the account ratio at 1.26 says the crowd is still net long, so the structural trapdoor below has not gone away, it has simply been refilled a few hundred points higher.

scalpContext.intradayBias: Breakout that is roughly three hours old and already 761.4 points extended off the end-of-day mark. Spot sits 564.09 over the 1H EMA20 at 78,767.31, which is a long way from the pivot and a poor place to initiate. The clean structure is: 78,900.0 is the flip level - it was the add gate, it is now the shelf a healthy pullback should hold; 79,396.8 is the session and 24h high; 79,648.1 is the next real ceiling. Between 78,551.3 and 78,900.0 there is nothing but the vacuum the move left behind, so a retrace through that pocket will be fast and will look worse than it is. Scalping the middle of a spent squeeze is how the last four sessions lost money.

calibration.rollingRecord: 8 wins, 6 losses across the last 14 graded sessions - and the losing streak is broken at four. Since 07 September end of day the chain had been L, L, L, L: endday bought into a 733.5-point drop, midnight bought into a 119.5-point drop, morning trimmed 269.7 points early, midday's add graded flat. End of day 08 September then refused to spend and set two gates; the add gate fired and price is 761.4 points higher, so this grades a win on the gates. The pattern worth keeping: four consecutive fractional losses came from paying for entries INSIDE the 78,000-79,500 band, and the win came from writing a level down and waiting for a settled close through it.
calibration.note: End of day's two gates split, and the split is instructive. The 77,624.6 reduce gate required a settled 1H close below the level; the lowest settled hourly close since the 00:36 UTC snapshot was 78,636.7 at 03:00 UTC and the lowest low 78,551.3, so price came within 926.7 points and never threatened it - the gate refused correctly, and end of day was right to resist the temptation it named, which was pulling the gate up to the 78,265.0 flush low. Had it done so, the 03:00 UTC candle low of 78,551.3 would still have missed, but the margin would have been 286.3 points instead of 926.7. The 78,900.0 add gate FIRED on the settled 04:00 UTC close of 79,169.0, 269.0 points through, and was confirmed by 78,935.1 at 05:00 and 79,160.3 at 06:00. The 77,432.19 invalidation was never approached and the recommended 77,580.0 resting stop was never within 971.0 points. So a trader who obeyed end of day's instructions bought the reclaim at 79,169.0 and marks 79,331.4, up 162.4 points. Where end of day graded imperfectly is the discretionary side: it chose HOLD and kept 23.20 USDT dry, so its own fired gate went untraded. Its stated reason - that the open-interest fall it required had arrived twice at four times the strength while price paid nothing, and that funding and the account ratio said the trapdoor was being rebuilt - was analytically sound and is still sound (open interest has since RISEN 0.70 percent and funding 13.03 percent). It was simply the wrong call for the next six hours. The lesson recorded for the wallet: a written gate that fires deserves a tranche even when the positioning read argues against it, because the gate is the falsifiable part and the positioning read is not.
